title: Gardening basics
examples: What kind of soil is best for tomatoes?
How deep should I plant a seed?
If it rains a lot, how much should I water?

explain.say: Today we learn about growing plants like little gardeners.
First we need good soil for our seeds to start in.
Plants need plenty of sunshine to make their food.
We must water plants when the soil feels dry and thirsty.
To grow a plant from seed, you plant it gently in the soil.
In real life, you can grow herbs like mint in a pot.

faq.q: How deep should I plant the seed?
faq.a: You should plant the seed just under the surface of the soil. This keeps it safe and moist for starting.
asks: How deep is good for seeds?
Should I bury the seed deep?

faq.q: How often should seedlings be watered?
faq.a: You should check the soil first; water only when the top layer feels dry to the touch. Overwatering can actually harm young plants.
asks: Is it okay to water every day?

faq.q: What is the best type of soil?
faq.a: A mix of compost, sand, and soil works very well for most garden plants. This mix helps the roots breathe easily.
asks: What soil mix do plants like?
Can I just use dirt from the ground?

faq.q: Do all plants need the same amount of sun?
faq.a: No, some plants like full sun, while others prefer shade. You must check what your specific plant needs.
asks: Do all plants need bright sun?
Some plants need less light, right?

faq.q: What if my seeds don't sprout?
faq.a: If seeds do not sprout, it might be because the soil is too hard or there is not enough warmth. Try warming the soil slightly.
asks: What if nothing happens after planting?

facts: Seeds need soil, sun, and water to begin growing.
Compost is excellent for improving the structure of soil.
Young seedlings need consistent moisture, but not constant soaking.
Most vegetables need at least six hours of direct sunlight daily.

quiz.say: What is the primary function of compost in garden soil?

options.show: It adds nutrients to the soil.
options.say: It adds nutrients to the soil.

options.show: It keeps the soil from drying out completely.
options.say: It keeps the soil from drying out completely.

options.show: It helps the roots grow deeper into the earth.
options.say: It helps the roots grow deeper into the earth.

options.show: It prevents weeds from growing nearby.
options.say: It prevents weeds from growing nearby.

quiz.why: Compost is decomposed organic matter that feeds the soil slowly over time.

wrong.1: This is true, but its main job is feeding, not just holding water.
wrong.2: This is a benefit, but 'adding nutrients' is the most direct function.
wrong.3: Compost is not a weed killer; it feeds the good things.

quiz.say: If the soil is very dry, what should you do first?

options.show: Pour water quickly over the top.
options.say: Pour water quickly over the top.

options.show: Water gently at the base of the plant.
options.say: Water gently at the base of the plant.

options.show: Spray the leaves with a hose.
options.say: Spray the leaves with a hose.

options.show: Wait until the next day to water.
options.say: Wait until the next day to water.

quiz.why: Watering at the base ensures the roots get the moisture they need without washing away.

wrong.0: Pouring too fast can cause runoff and not soak into the soil.
wrong.2: This can wash away pollen or encourage leaf diseases.
wrong.3: If it is very dry, waiting might let the roots become too stressed.

quiz.say: Which combination is essential for germination?

options.show: Watering every day and bright sun.
options.say: Watering every day and bright sun.

quiz.why: Seeds need a stable environment containing physical support, warmth, and water to start life.

wrong.0: Rain is good, but seeds also need warmth and structure from the soil.
wrong.1: Too much water without good soil can actually drown the tiny seeds.
wrong.3: Seeds need more than just light; they need something to anchor into.
